name: crawl4ai
solution: Its HTTP-only crawler strategy fetches the page and its CSS extraction strategy reads each country as text, then a short loop converts the numbers and the missing capital. The crawl is its breadth-first deep crawl with the same extraction strategy. No browser is downloaded or started. Its home folder, where it keeps logs and a robots.txt cache, is moved into the benchmark's cache.

footnotes.text: crawl4ai's breadth-first crawl never marks the entry page as visited, so every page that links back to it queues it again. A filter keeps it out. Without the filter the entry page is fetched twice, and the second fetch uses one of the 20 pages, so a country page is left out.
At its defaults crawl4ai runs up to five fetches at once, with a random delay of 0.1 to 0.4 s per host that doesn't carry over from one level to the next, so some requests reach the server together.
crawl4ai's `crwl` command line does the task in one line, but it always starts a browser, so that line isn't counted. The count is for the Python solution, which uses the HTTP-only crawler strategy.
crawl4ai requires Playwright and Patchright even for its HTTP-only strategy, so no smaller install exists. They take 110 MB each because each bundles a Node driver. No browser is downloaded.
